text:
tara: heads up — ran into a reproducible interop problem when using the JS SDK inside an edge-target app built with Vite (webworker) + webpack for parts of our infra. Dev server ok; production worker throws either `ReferenceError: require is not defined` or `TypeError: Redwood.default is not a function`.

tara: minimal repro I used:
1) create vite typescript app (vanilla-ts)
2) set vite build target to webworker (target: 'es2020')
3) install local packed SDK tar (`npm i ../packages/redwood-sdk-0.0.0.tgz`)
4) `import Redwood from 'redwood-inference-js'` in main.ts and run `vite build && vite preview` -> worker crash in console.

ben: did you inspect the package.json fields of the published SDK? bundlers make different choices based on `exports`, `module`, `main`, and `browser` fields.

tara: yes. published SDK has `main: ./dist/index.cjs.js`, `module: ./dist/index.esm.js`, and an `exports` map with `import` -> `./dist/index.esm.js`, `require` -> `./dist/index.cjs.js`. The cjs build contains top-level `require()` calls that obviously fail in ESM-only edge runtimes.

inga: this is a classic conditional exports resolution mismatch. Vite's optimizeDeps or SSR resolution sometimes resolves the require side for edge builds. Did you try consumer-side fixes like `optimizeDeps.include` or `ssr.noExternal`?

tara: yes. `optimizeDeps.include = ['redwood-inference-js']` fixes dev prebundling in many cases, and `ssr.noExternal` helps server builds, but the final worker bundle still ended up with references to the cjs file in some configs.

ben: two practical SDK fixes we should consider: 1) make the ESM/browser entry unambiguous (add `browser` field and `exports."./browser"` mapping), 2) ship an explicit tiny edge entrypoint e.g. `dist/edge.mjs` that re-exports the ESM bundle and map `exports."./edge"` to it so consumers can `import 'redwood-inference-js/edge'`.

inga: also watch out for how the ESM build is produced. If rollup/tsc emit tiny cjs-interop wrappers (even comments or `__require` helpers), some resolvers will still treat the artifact as CJS. Linting `dist/index.esm.js` for `require(`, `module.exports`, or `exports.` and failing CI if present would catch regressions.

ci-bot: nightly/sdk-bundle: failing matrix entry `worker/vite` -> runtime ReferenceError: require is not defined. See logs (internal).

tara: temporary consumer workaround I used to unblock teams: import the ESM file directly `import Redwood from 'redwood-inference-js/dist/index.esm.js'` or from the shim `import Redwood from 'redwood-inference-js/dist/edge.mjs'` if we publish that. Not ideal but works.

ben: long-term, add a CI job that `pnpm pack` the SDK, then installs it into three tiny consumer templates (vite webworker, webpack worker, rollup worker) and runs the built worker in a lightweight emulator (miniflare/wrangler). Fail when runtime shows `require is not defined` or default import shape errors.

inga: also verify d.ts output: our current bundled types sometimes use `export =` style which confuses consumers with different TS `esModuleInterop` settings. Generate types that match the ESM shape (`export default` plus named exports) to prevent mismatches that lead to runtime shape differences.

tara: filed an SDK issue with repro repo and configs (link in internal ticket). assigning to eng-platform for package/CI changes and eng-runtime for build audit. I'll add a short note to the DX guide documenting `optimizeDeps.include` and `ssr.noExternal` as temporary mitigations and point to the issue.
